items.stem: Inside an ultra-high-vacuum electrostatic calibration chamber, two fixed point charges of +3 nC (left) and −6 nC (right) are held 0.6 m apart. Point P lies on the straight line joining them at a distance of 0.2 m to the right of the +3 nC charge. Use 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² throughout. What is the resultant electric field strength and direction at P?
items.workedSolution: At P, both opposite-sign sources drive a positive test charge to the right. |E₁| = k|q₁|/r₁² = 674 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/r₂² = 337 N C⁻¹ (with r₂ = 0.4 m). Summing the two same-sense vectors gives E = 1.01 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

markScheme.criterion: Adds same-direction inverse-square contributions to obtain 1.01 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

items.stem: Along the optical axis of a benchtop ion-trap demonstration rig, charges −4 nC and +8 nC are separated horizontally by 0.8 m, with −4 nC on the left. Observation point P is situated between them, 0.2 m from the left-hand source. Use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² for free-space electrostatic interactions. Determine the magnitude and direction of the net electric field at point P.
items.workedSolution: At P, both opposite-sign sources drive a positive test charge to the left. |E₁| = k|q₁|/r₁² = 899 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/r₂² = 200 N C⁻¹ (with r₂ = 0.6 m). Summing the two same-sense vectors gives E = 1.10 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (A).

markScheme.criterion: Adds same-direction inverse-square contributions to obtain 1.10 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (A).

items.stem: On an insulated fused-quartz metrology rail in vacuum, an axial probe point P sits 0.2 m from a left-hand +5 nC point charge along the 0.5 m segment connecting it to a right-hand −4 nC point charge. Take the Coulomb constant as k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Which row gives the magnitude and direction of the electric field vector at P?
items.workedSolution: At P, both opposite-sign sources drive a positive test charge to the right. |E₁| = k|q₁|/r₁² = 1.12 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/r₂² = 400 N C⁻¹ (with r₂ = 0.3 m). Summing the two same-sense vectors gives E = 1.52 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (B).

markScheme.criterion: Adds same-direction inverse-square contributions to obtain 1.52 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (B).

items.stem: Within a shielded Faraday enclosure used for sensor testing, a point charge of −6 nC is fixed at x = 0 and a second point charge of +3 nC is fixed at x = 0.6 m. A field sensor is placed at point P on the axis at x = 0.3 m. Treat both sources as point charges in vacuum with k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Find the resultant electric field vector acting at point P.
items.workedSolution: At P, both opposite-sign sources drive a positive test charge to the left. |E₁| = k|q₁|/r₁² = 599 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/r₂² = 300 N C⁻¹ (with r₂ = 0.3 m). Summing the two same-sense vectors gives E = 899 N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

markScheme.criterion: Adds same-direction inverse-square contributions to obtain 899 N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

items.stem: In a dry-nitrogen micro-electrostatics apparatus, two fixed point charges of −8 nC (left) and +5 nC (right) are held 0.7 m apart. Point P lies on the straight line joining them at a distance of 0.3 m to the right of the −8 nC charge. Assume vacuum permittivity such that k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². markScheme.criterion: Adds same-direction inverse-square contributions to obtain 1.08 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

items.stem: On a sapphire isolation substrate inside a cleanroom vacuum stage, two fixed point charges of +8 nC (left) and −4 nC (right) are held 0.6 m apart. Point P lies on the straight line joining them at a distance of 0.4 m to the right of the +8 nC charge. Treat both sources as point charges in vacuum with k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Which row gives the magnitude and direction of the electric field vector at P?
items.workedSolution: At P, both opposite-sign sources drive a positive test charge to the right. |E₁| = k|q₁|/r₁² = 449 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/r₂² = 899 N C⁻¹ (with r₂ = 0.2 m). Summing the two same-sense vectors gives E = 1.35 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

markScheme.criterion: Adds same-direction inverse-square contributions to obtain 1.35 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, along a 0.5 m baseline between fixed charges +8 nC on the left and +2 nC on the right, point P lies 0.2 m from the left source. markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 1.60 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Along the reference baseline of an electrostatic beam-steering rig, along a 0.5 m baseline between fixed charges +3 nC on the left and +12 nC on the right, point P lies 0.3 m from the left source. items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.3)² = 300 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.2)² = 2.70 × 10³ N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 2.40 × 10³ N C⁻¹ directed to the left (B).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 2.40 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (B).

items.stem: Across the measurement track of a non-contact Kelvin probe bench, fixed point charges −5 nC (at x = 0) and −15 nC (at x = 0.9 m) occupy a straight insulating rail. Point P is situated at x = 0.6 m. Treat both sources as point charges in vacuum with k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Determine the resultant electric field strength and sense at P.
items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.6)² = 125 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.3)² = 1.50 × 10³ N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 1.37 × 10³ N C⁻¹ directed to the right (A).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 1.37 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Inside an electrostatic aerosol-charging test section, along a 0.7 m baseline between fixed charges +7 nC on the left and +3 nC on the right, point P lies 0.3 m from the left source. Use 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² throughout. What is the resultant electric field at point P?
items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.3)² = 699 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.4)² = 169 N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 531 N C⁻¹ directed to the right (B).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 531 N C⁻¹ to the right (B).

items.stem: Along the symmetry line of a miniature ion-optics bench, a left-hand source of +4 nC and a right-hand source of +16 nC are separated by 0.8 m. An axial test point P is located 0.5 m to the right of +4 nC. Model the region as vacuum with Coulomb constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Calculate the magnitude and direction of the resultant electric field at P.
items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.5)² = 144 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.3)² = 1.60 × 10³ N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 1.45 × 10³ N C⁻¹ directed to the left (C).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 1.45 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

items.stem: Within a laboratory quadrupole pre-alignment vacuum housing, two like-sign point charges of −9 nC and −2 nC are fixed 0.5 m apart, with −9 nC on the left. Point P lies on the connecting axis 0.2 m from the left charge. Use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² for free-space electrostatic interactions. Which option states the net electric field vector at P?
items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.2)² = 2.02 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.3)² = 200 N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 1.82 × 10³ N C⁻¹ directed to the left (D).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 1.82 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

items.stem: Within an evacuated spacecraft charge-control test cell, a point charge +12 nC is fixed at x = 0 and a second point charge −3 nC is fixed at x = 0.3 m. Exterior point P lies further to the right along the positive x-axis at x = 0.5 m (so P is 0.2 m to the right of −3 nC). Treat both sources as point charges in vacuum with k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electric field at exterior point P?
items.workedSolution: Exterior point P is r₁ = 0.5 m to the right of +12 nC and r₂ = 0.5 − 0.3 = 0.2 m to the right of −3 nC. Superposing E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂² gives 243 N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 0.5 m and r₂ = 0.2 m to obtain 243 N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

items.stem: On a sapphire isolation substrate inside a cleanroom vacuum stage, two collinear point charges of −9 nC (left) and +4 nC (right) are separated by 0.4 m. Point P lies outside the pair to the right of both charges, at a total distance of 0.6 m from the left-hand −9 nC charge. Adopt the free-space constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electric field at exterior point P?
items.workedSolution: Exterior point P is r₁ = 0.6 m to the right of −9 nC and r₂ = 0.6 − 0.4 = 0.2 m to the right of +4 nC. Superposing E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂² gives 674 N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Along the symmetry line of a miniature ion-optics bench, a point charge −12 nC is fixed at x = 0 and a second point charge +5 nC is fixed at x = 0.4 m. Exterior point P lies further to the right along the positive x-axis at x = 0.7 m (so P is 0.3 m to the right of +5 nC). Adopt the free-space constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electric field at exterior point P?
items.workedSolution: Exterior point P is r₁ = 0.7 m to the right of −12 nC and r₂ = 0.7 − 0.4 = 0.3 m to the right of +5 nC. Superposing E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂² gives 279 N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 0.7 m and r₂ = 0.3 m to obtain 279 N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

items.stem: Inside a university physics Van de Graaff calibration tunnel, positive point charges +2Q (on the left) and +4Q (on the right) are fixed a distance 3 x apart in vacuum. Point P lies on the line joining them at a distance 1 x from +2Q (and 2 x from +4Q). Using Coulomb constant k, what is the resultant electric field at P expressed in terms of kQ/x²?
items.workedSolution: At P, +2Q produces (2/1²) kQ/x² = 2.00 kQ/x² to the right, while +4Q at distance 2 x produces (4/2²) kQ/x² = 1.00 kQ/x² to the left. Net field = 1.00 kQ/x² to the right (D).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts (2/1²) and (4/2²) to obtain 1.00 kQ/x² to the right (D).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts (3/1²) and (8/2²) to obtain 1.00 kQ/x² to the right (A).

items.stem: Within a shielded Faraday enclosure used for sensor testing, two fixed source charges of +4 nC (left) and −8 nC (right) are separated by 0.6 m. Point P lies on the line joining them, 0.2 m from the left source. A small probe charge of −2.5 nC is placed at P without disturbing the fixed sources. items.workedSolution: At P (r₁ = 0.2 m, r₂ = 0.4 m), the resultant electric field is E = 1.35 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right. Multiplying by q_test = −2.5 nC gives F = q_test E = 3.37 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left (D).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = 1.35 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and F = qE = 3.37 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left (D).

items.stem: Along a straight dielectric mounting rod inside an evacuated bell jar, stationary point charges +6 nC (left) and −3 nC (right) are mounted 0.5 m apart, with axial point P located 0.2 m from the left charge. A small probe charge of −4 nC is placed at P without disturbing the fixed sources. Adopt the free-space constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electrostatic force acting on the −4 nC probe charge?
items.workedSolution: At P (r₁ = 0.2 m, r₂ = 0.3 m), the resultant electric field is E = 1.65 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right. Multiplying by q_test = −4 nC gives F = q_test E = 6.59 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left (A).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = 1.65 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and F = qE = 6.59 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left (A).

items.stem: In a dry-nitrogen micro-electrostatics apparatus, along a 0.6 m vacuum baseline between fixed charges −5 nC on the left and +10 nC on the right, point P is marked 0.3 m from −5 nC. A small probe charge of −3 nC is placed at P without disturbing the fixed sources. Model the region as vacuum with Coulomb constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electrostatic force acting on the −3 nC probe charge?
items.workedSolution: At P (r₁ = 0.3 m, r₂ = 0.3 m), the resultant electric field is E = 1.50 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left. Multiplying by q_test = −3 nC gives F = q_test E = 4.50 × 10⁻⁶ N to the right (B).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = 1.50 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and F = qE = 4.50 × 10⁻⁶ N to the right (B).

items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, source charges +8 nC at x = 0 and +2 nC at x = 0.5 m are held stationary, while point P sits on the axis at x = 0.2 m. A small probe charge of −2 nC is placed at P without disturbing the fixed sources. Take the Coulomb constant as k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electrostatic force acting on the −2 nC probe charge?
items.workedSolution: At P (r₁ = 0.2 m, r₂ = 0.3 m), the resultant electric field is E = 1.60 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right. Multiplying by q_test = −2 nC gives F = q_test E = 3.20 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left (C).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = 1.60 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and F = qE = 3.20 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left (C).

items.stem: Inside a cryogenic linear Paul-trap alignment fixture, two fixed source charges of +3 nC (left) and −9 nC (right) are separated by 0.6 m. Point P lies on the line joining them, 0.3 m from the left source. A small probe charge of +2.5 nC is placed at P without disturbing the fixed sources. Use 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² throughout. What is the resultant electrostatic force acting on the +2.5 nC probe charge?
items.workedSolution: At P (r₁ = 0.3 m, r₂ = 0.3 m), the resultant electric field is E = 1.20 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right. Multiplying by q_test = +2.5 nC gives F = q_test E = 3.00 × 10⁻⁶ N to the right (D).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = 1.20 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and F = qE = 3.00 × 10⁻⁶ N to the right (D).

items.stem: Along the central axis of a precision Coulomb torsion module, stationary point charges −4 nC (left) and +6 nC (right) are mounted 0.5 m apart, with axial point P located 0.2 m from the left charge. A small probe charge of +3.5 nC is placed at P without disturbing the fixed sources. Assume vacuum permittivity such that k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electrostatic force acting on the +3.5 nC probe charge?
items.workedSolution: At P (r₁ = 0.2 m, r₂ = 0.3 m), the resultant electric field is E = 1.50 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left. Multiplying by q_test = +3.5 nC gives F = q_test E = 5.24 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left (A).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates E = 1.50 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and F = qE = 5.24 × 10⁻⁶ N to the left (A).

items.stem: Inside a cryogenic linear Paul-trap alignment fixture, isolated point charges +4 nC at x = 0 and +9 nC at x = 0.5 m are mounted along a straight insulating track. At what distance from the +4 nC charge along the line joining the charges is the resultant electric field equal to zero?
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes gives q₁/x² = q₂/(0.5 − x)², so (0.5 − x)/x = √(9/4). Solving yields x = 0.5 × √4/(√4 + √9) = 0.200 m (D).

markScheme.criterion: Equates kq₁/x² = kq₂/(0.5 − x)² to obtain x = 0.200 m (D).

items.stem: Along the central axis of a precision Coulomb torsion module, along a 0.6 m baseline in free space, a +1 nC point charge is fixed at the left end and a +4 nC point charge is fixed at the right end. markScheme.criterion: Equates kq₁/x² = kq₂/(0.6 − x)² to obtain x = 0.200 m (A).

items.stem: On a sapphire isolation substrate inside a cleanroom vacuum stage, along a 0.9 m baseline in free space, a +2 nC point charge is fixed at the left end and a +8 nC point charge is fixed at the right end. At what distance from the +2 nC charge along the line joining the charges is the resultant electric field equal to zero?
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes gives q₁/x² = q₂/(0.9 − x)², so (0.9 − x)/x = √(8/2). Solving yields x = 0.9 × √2/(√2 + √8) = 0.300 m (C).

markScheme.criterion: Equates kq₁/x² = kq₂/(0.9 − x)² to obtain x = 0.300 m (C).

items.stem: Within a dust-plasma levitation chamber evacuated to low pressure, two fixed point charges q₁ and q₂ are separated by 0.6 m in vacuum, with q₁ = 4 × 10⁻⁹ C on the left. Measurements along the connecting axis show that the resultant electric field is zero at a distance of 0.2 m from q₁. What is the signed charge q₂?
items.workedSolution: An interior null point requires q₁ and q₂ to have the same sign (+). Equating kq₁/x₀² = kq₂/(d − x₀)² with d − x₀ = 0.4 m gives q₂ = q₁((0.4)/(0.2))² = 4.00 × 4 × 10⁻⁹ C = +1.60 × 10⁻⁸ C (A).

markScheme.criterion: Uses q₂ = q₁((d − x₀)/x₀)² with positive sign to obtain +1.60 × 10⁻⁸ C (A).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ((d − x₀)/x₀)² = (0.6/0.2)² = 9.00 (B).

items.stem: On an insulated fused-quartz metrology rail in vacuum, a point charge q₁ = 1.6 × 10⁻⁸ C sits at x = 0 and an unknown point charge q₂ sits at x = 0.9 m. An axial field scan locates a zero-field null point between them at x = 0.6 m. What is the magnitude ratio |q₂ / q₁|?
items.workedSolution: At x₀ = 0.6 m, the distance from q₂ is d − x₀ = 0.3 m. Setting |q₁|/x₀² = |q₂|/(d − x₀)² gives |q₂/q₁| = (0.3/0.6)² = 0.250 (A).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ((d − x₀)/x₀)² = (0.3/0.6)² = 0.250 (A).

items.stem: Within a shielded Faraday enclosure used for sensor testing, fixed sources q₁ (left, 2.5 × 10⁻⁹ C) and q₂ (right) lie 0.45 m apart. The electric field vanishes at an interior point 0.15 m to the right of q₁. What is the signed charge q₂?
items.workedSolution: An interior null point requires q₁ and q₂ to have the same sign (+). Equating kq₁/x₀² = kq₂/(d − x₀)² with d − x₀ = 0.3 m gives q₂ = q₁((0.3)/(0.15))² = 4.00 × 2.5 × 10⁻⁹ C = +1.00 × 10⁻⁸ C (B).

markScheme.criterion: Uses q₂ = q₁((d − x₀)/x₀)² with positive sign to obtain +1.00 × 10⁻⁸ C (B).

items.stem: In a dry-nitrogen micro-electrostatics apparatus, two fixed point charges q₁ and q₂ are separated by 0.5 m in vacuum, with q₁ = 9 × 10⁻⁹ C on the left. Measurements along the connecting axis show that the resultant electric field is zero at a distance of 0.3 m from q₁. What is the signed charge q₂?
items.workedSolution: An interior null point requires q₁ and q₂ to have the same sign (+). Equating kq₁/x₀² = kq₂/(d − x₀)² with d − x₀ = 0.2 m gives q₂ = q₁((0.2)/(0.3))² = 0.444 × 9 × 10⁻⁹ C = +4.00 × 10⁻⁹ C (D).

markScheme.criterion: Uses q₂ = q₁((d − x₀)/x₀)² with positive sign to obtain +4.00 × 10⁻⁹ C (D).

items.stem: In a time-of-flight mass spectrometer extraction stage, two parallel conducting plates separated by 0.03 m are maintained at a potential difference of 240 V (from 240 V on the left plate to 0 V on the right plate). A positively charged droplet of charge +2.5 × 10⁻⁸ C and mass 4 × 10⁻⁶ kg is released at the 240 V plate. Ignore edge effects. What is the magnitude of the uniform electric field between the plates?
items.workedSolution: For uniform parallel plates, E = V / d = 240 / 0.03 = 8.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Inside a cathode-ray oscilloscope vertical deflection assembly, a potential difference of 400 V is applied across parallel planar electrodes spaced 0.05 m apart. A test micro-sphere carrying charge +3 × 10⁻⁸ C and mass 5 × 10⁻⁶ kg crosses from the positive electrode to the grounded 0 V electrode. items.workedSolution: Electrical work done across the full potential difference is W = qΔV = (3 × 10⁻⁸)(400) = 1.20 × 10⁻⁵ J (B).

items.stem: Across the uniform-field region of a parallel-plate guard-ring cell, a uniform electrostatic gap of width 0.05 m operates with 1500 V across its parallel plates while a carrier (q = +6 × 10⁻⁹ C, m = 4.5 × 10⁻⁶ kg) traverses from the high-potential plate to the 0 V plate. How much electrical work is done by the electric field on the particle as it crosses from the 1500 V plate to the 0 V plate?
items.workedSolution: Electrical work done across the full potential difference is W = qΔV = (6 × 10⁻⁹)(1500) = 9.00 × 10⁻⁶ J (A).

items.stem: Within a laboratory positron-moderation extraction stage, inside an evacuated cell of gap width 0.015 m biased at 180 V, a charged aerosol particle of mass 1.5 × 10⁻⁶ kg and charge +2 × 10⁻⁸ C travels from the +180 V electrode to the 0 V collector. Neglecting fringing at the plate edges, calculate the uniform electric field strength in the gap.
items.workedSolution: For uniform parallel plates, E = V / d = 180 / 0.015 = 1.20 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Between polished aluminium plates in an evacuated deflection tube, flat parallel plates spaced 0.06 m apart establish a 720 V potential drop as a micro-carrier (mass 5 × 10⁻⁶ kg, charge +2.5 × 10⁻⁸ C) moves from the positive plate to the earthed 0 V plate. What kinetic energy (in joules) is transferred to the carrier by the electric field across the 720 V potential drop?
items.workedSolution: Electrical work done across the full potential difference is W = qΔV = (2.5 × 10⁻⁸)(720) = 1.80 × 10⁻⁵ J (C).

items.workedSolution: For uniform parallel plates, E = V / d = 2000 / 0.04 = 5.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Across the planar extraction electrodes of a surface-analysis gun, a potential difference of 450 V is applied across parallel planar electrodes spaced 0.03 m apart. A test micro-sphere carrying charge +6 × 10⁻⁹ C and mass 3 × 10⁻⁶ kg crosses from the positive electrode to the grounded 0 V electrode. Determine the electrical work performed by the uniform field during the full transit to the 0 V electrode.
items.workedSolution: Electrical work done across the full potential difference is W = qΔV = (6 × 10⁻⁹)(450) = 2.70 × 10⁻⁶ J (A).

items.stem: Within a medical linear-accelerator pre-injector gap, a proton (charge +0 C, mass 0 kg) starts from rest at a planar electrode at +500 V and accelerates in vacuum across a 0.04 m gap to a parallel grounded electrode at 0 V. Neglecting gravity, what speed does the proton reach upon arriving at the 0 V plate?
items.workedSolution: By conservation of energy, ½mv² = qV, so v = √(2qV / m) = √(2 × 0 × 500 / 0) = 3.10 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (A).

markScheme.criterion: Equates ½mv² = qV to obtain v = 3.10 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: On an insulated fused-quartz metrology rail in vacuum, point charges +6 nC (left) and −4 nC (right) are fixed 0.5 m apart, and point P lies on the line between them 0.2 m from +6 nC. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and define electric potential to be zero at infinity. What is the electric potential at point P?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential is a signed scalar: V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂) with r₁ = 0.2 m and r₂ = 0.3 m. Thus V = 270 V + (−120 V) = 150 V (A).

items.stem: Within a shielded Faraday enclosure used for sensor testing, two stationary charges of −8 nC on the left and +3 nC on the right have separation 0.6 m, with point P marked 0.2 m from the left source. items.workedSolution: Electric potential is a signed scalar: V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂) with r₁ = 0.2 m and r₂ = 0.4 m. Thus V = −360 V + (67.4 V) = −292 V (B).

markScheme.criterion: Sums signed scalar potentials kq₁/0.2 + kq₂/0.4 = −292 V (B).

items.workedSolution: Electric potential is a signed scalar: V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂) with r₁ = 0.3 m and r₂ = 0.3 m. Thus V = 270 V + (−89.9 V) = 180 V (B).

markScheme.criterion: Sums signed scalar potentials kq₁/0.3 + kq₂/0.3 = 180 V (B).

items.stem: Along the central axis of a precision Coulomb torsion module, point charges −10 nC (left) and +4 nC (right) are fixed 0.7 m apart, and point P lies on the line between them 0.3 m from −10 nC. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and define electric potential to be zero at infinity. What is the electric potential at point P?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential is a signed scalar: V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂) with r₁ = 0.3 m and r₂ = 0.4 m. Thus V = −300 V + (89.9 V) = −210 V (C).

markScheme.criterion: Sums signed scalar potentials kq₁/0.3 + kq₂/0.4 = −210 V (C).

Assume vacuum (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²) and reference all scalar potentials to zero at infinity. What is the electric potential at point P?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential is a signed scalar: V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂) with r₁ = 0.4 m and r₂ = 0.2 m. Thus V = 67.4 V + (−450 V) = −382 V (A).

markScheme.criterion: Sums signed scalar potentials kq₁/0.4 + kq₂/0.2 = −382 V (A).

items.stem: Inside a university physics Van de Graaff calibration tunnel, point charges +12 nC (left) and −5 nC (right) are fixed 0.8 m apart, and point P lies on the line between them 0.3 m from +12 nC. Adopt k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and zero electrostatic potential at infinite distance. What is the electric potential at point P?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential is a signed scalar: V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂) with r₁ = 0.3 m and r₂ = 0.5 m. Thus V = 360 V + (−89.9 V) = 270 V (B).

markScheme.criterion: Sums signed scalar potentials kq₁/0.3 + kq₂/0.5 = 270 V (B).

items.stem: Along the reference baseline of an electrostatic beam-steering rig, opposite point charges +4 nC (left) and −4 nC (right) are fixed 0.4 m apart. Point P lies on the connecting axis 0.2 m from +4 nC, where the scalar electric potential vanishes. Assume vacuum (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²) and reference all scalar potentials to zero at infinity. Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the right: E = 899 N C⁻¹ + 899 N C⁻¹ = 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Along the symmetry line of a miniature ion-optics bench, two opposite-sign sources of −9 nC on the left and +3 nC on the right have separation 0.8 m; axial point P is situated 0.6 m from −9 nC. items.stem: Along the optical axis of a benchtop ion-trap demonstration rig, along the 1 m line segment between −5 nC (left) and +15 nC (right), point P sits 0.25 m from the left source. Use 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² with the reference of zero potential at infinite separation. Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the left: E = 719 N C⁻¹ + 240 N C⁻¹ = 959 N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 959 N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

items.stem: On an insulated fused-quartz metrology rail in vacuum, opposite point charges +9 nC (left) and −9 nC (right) are fixed 0.6 m apart. Point P lies on the connecting axis 0.3 m from +9 nC, where the scalar electric potential vanishes. Assume vacuum (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²) and reference all scalar potentials to zero at infinity. Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the right: E = 899 N C⁻¹ + 899 N C⁻¹ = 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

items.stem: Inside an electrostatic aerosol-charging test section, stationary charges +2 nC (on the left) and +18 nC (on the right) sit at separation 0.8 m. Model the charges in free space (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²), taking V = 0 at infinity. What is the electric potential at the unique point on the line between the charges where the resultant electric field is zero?
items.workedSolution: Zero field occurs at x = 0.8 × √2/(√2 + √18) = 0.200 m from +2 nC (and 0.600 m from +18 nC). Scalar potentials add: V = k(q₁/x + q₂/(d − x)) = 360 V (A).

markScheme.criterion: Finds x = 0.200 m and sums positive scalar potentials to obtain 360 V (A).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = k(q₁/0.2 + q₂/0.4) = 44.9 V (A), independent of q_test.

Adopt k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and zero electrostatic potential at infinite distance. What is the electric potential at P due to the two fixed source charges?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = k(q₁/0.3 + q₂/0.5) = −192 V (A), independent of q_test.

items.stem: An electrostatic field plotter maps three parallel vertical equipotential surfaces labelled from left to right as -200 V, -80 V, and 40 V with uniform spacing 0.08 m between neighbouring surfaces. A test charge of +3 × 10⁻⁸ C is displaced from the leftmost surface (-200 V) to the rightmost surface (40 V). What is the signed change in electrostatic potential energy ΔE_p of the charge?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE_p = q(V_f − V_i) = 7.20 × 10⁻⁶ J (D).

items.stem: Inside a uniform-field drift chamber, three equally spaced planar equipotential lines are recorded at 360 V (left), 200 V (middle), and 40 V (right), with adjacent lines separated by 0.05 m. markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W_field = q(V_i − V_f) = −4.00 × 10⁻⁶ J (A).

items.stem: Across the central region of a wide guard-ring capacitor, three vertical equipotential lines are drawn at 240 V (left), 140 V (middle), and 40 V (right), with adjacent lines spaced 0.05 m apart. A charged dielectric bead of mass 2 × 10⁻⁵ kg and charge +4 × 10⁻⁸ C starts from rest on the middle 140 V line and moves frictionlessly horizontally to the 40 V line. What is the magnitude and direction of the uniform electric field?
items.workedSolution: Electric field points toward decreasing potential (to the right) with magnitude E = |ΔV|/s = (140 − 40) / 0.05 = 2.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ to the right (B).

markScheme.criterion: Uses E = −ΔV/Δx to obtain 2.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ to the right (B).

What is the magnitude of the horizontal electrostatic acceleration of the charged dielectric bead?

markScheme.criterion: Finds E = 3.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ and a = qE/m = 5.00 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: A Kelvin-probe scan across a uniform electrostatic region identifies three parallel equipotential lines at 400 V (left), 250 V (middle), and 100 V (right), with adjacent lines spaced 0.03 m apart. A charged dielectric bead of mass 5 × 10⁻⁵ kg and charge +3 × 10⁻⁸ C starts from rest on the middle 250 V line and moves frictionlessly horizontally to the 100 V line. What is the magnitude and direction of the uniform electric field?
items.workedSolution: Electric field points toward decreasing potential (to the right) with magnitude E = |ΔV|/s = (250 − 100) / 0.03 = 5.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ to the right (D).

markScheme.criterion: Uses E = −ΔV/Δx to obtain 5.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ to the right (D).

items.stem: Within an evacuated deflection cell, three parallel equipotential planes are maintained at 280 V (left), 160 V (middle), and 40 V (right), with adjacent lines spaced 0.03 m apart. A charged dielectric bead of mass 2.7 × 10⁻⁵ kg and charge +4.5 × 10⁻⁸ C starts from rest on the middle 160 V line and moves frictionlessly horizontally to the 40 V line. What is the magnitude and direction of the uniform electric field?
items.workedSolution: Electric field points toward decreasing potential (to the right) with magnitude E = |ΔV|/s = (160 − 40) / 0.03 = 4.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ to the right (B).

markScheme.criterion: Uses E = −ΔV/Δx to obtain 4.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ to the right (B).

markScheme.criterion: Finds E = 5.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ and a = qE/m = 20.0 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: In a head-on Rutherford backscattering experiment, a projectile alpha particle of charge +2e approaches head-on a stationary gold nucleus of atomic number Z = 79 (charge +79e) to a distance of closest approach r_min = 4.5 × 10⁻¹⁴ m. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and zero electric potential at infinity. What is the electric potential due to the gold nucleus at distance r_min?
items.workedSolution: Radial potential of the +79e nucleus is V = kZe / r_min = (8.99 × 10⁹ × 79 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) / (4.5 × 10⁻¹⁴) = 2.53 × 10⁶ V (B).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = kZe / r_min = 2.53 × 10⁶ V (B).

items.stem: During a nuclear physics beamline scattering run, an incident alpha particle carrying charge +2e reaches a minimum centre-to-centre separation of 3.6 × 10⁻¹⁴ m from a heavy silver nucleus of charge +47e. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and zero electric potential at infinity. What is the electrostatic potential energy of the system at closest approach, expressed in electronvolts (eV)?
items.workedSolution: At r_min, V = kZe / r_min = 1.88 × 10⁶ V. For a +2e projectile, E_p = 2eV = 3.76 × 10⁶ eV (C).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = 1.88 × 10⁶ V and E_p = 2V (in eV) = 3.76 × 10⁶ eV (C).

items.stem: Within an evacuated target chamber at a tandem accelerator, a projectile alpha particle of charge +2e approaches head-on a stationary copper nucleus of atomic number Z = 29 (charge +29e) to a distance of closest approach r_min = 2.8 × 10⁻¹⁴ m. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and zero electric potential at infinity. What is the electrostatic potential energy of the system at closest approach, expressed in electronvolts (eV)?
items.workedSolution: At r_min, V = kZe / r_min = 1.49 × 10⁶ V. For a +2e projectile, E_p = 2eV = 2.98 × 10⁶ eV (A).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = 1.49 × 10⁶ V and E_p = 2V (in eV) = 2.98 × 10⁶ eV (A).

parts.prompt: State and explain why the two individual electric field contributions reinforce rather than oppose each other at point P.
parts.expectedAnswer: Both individual electric field vectors at P point to the left (toward the negative left source and away from the positive right source), so they reinforce toward the left.
workingSteps: Electric field direction is the force direction on a positive test charge.
Both individual electric field vectors at P point to the left (toward the negative left source and away from the positive right source), so they reinforce toward the left.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude and state the direction of the resultant electric field at point P.
workingSteps: |E₁| = k|q₁|/r₁² = 1.44 × 10³ N C⁻¹; |E₂| = k|q₂|/r₂² = 180 N C⁻¹.
Resultant E = |E₁| + |E₂| = 1.62 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left.

items.stem: Inside an electrostatic aerosol-charging test section, charges +3.5 nC and −7 nC are separated horizontally by 0.7 m, with +3.5 nC on the left. Observation point P is situated between them, 0.2 m from the left-hand source. Take the Coulomb constant as k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Both individual electric field vectors at P point to the right (away from the positive left source and toward the negative right source), so they reinforce toward the right. (b) With r₁ = 0.2 m and r₂ = 0.5 m, |E₁| = 787 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = 252 N C⁻¹. Summing gives 1.04 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: Explains using a positive test charge that both source fields at P act in the same direction.
Applies E = k|q|/r² with r₁ = 0.2 m and r₂ = 0.5 m.
Adds the two collinear field magnitudes.
Obtains 1.04 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right.

items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, on a straight vacuum baseline of total length 3 x between +8Q on the left and +5Q on the right, point P lies 2 x from the left source. Write the resultant electric field magnitude at P in the form E = α kQ/x², where k is the Coulomb constant.
items.workedSolution: (a) The right positive charge produces a larger repulsive field magnitude at P than the left positive charge, so the net electric field points to the left. (b) α = |8/2² − 5/1²| = |2.00 − 5.00| = 3.00.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant direction as to the left with valid reasoning.
Forms inverse-square terms 8/2² and 5/1².
Subtracts the opposing dimensionless field coefficients.
Obtains α = 3.00.

parts.prompt: Calculate the distance from the +9 nC charge to the zero-field point.

items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, a point charge q₁ = 2.5 × 10⁻⁸ C sits at x = 0 and an unknown point charge q₂ sits at x = 0.8 m. An axial field scan locates a zero-field null point between them at x = 0.5 m.
items.workedSolution: (a) q₁ and q₂ have the same sign so their fields oppose between them. (b) |q₂/q₁| = ((0.8 − 0.5)/0.5)² = (0.3/0.5)² = 0.360. (c) q₂ = +(0.360)(2.5 × 10⁻⁸ C) = +9.00 × 10⁻⁹ C.

markScheme.criterion: States same sign because fields must oppose in the region between the charges.
Uses |q₂/q₁| = ((d − x₀)/x₀)² with d − x₀ = 0.3 m.
Obtains 0.360.
Multiplies q₁ by ratio from (b) with positive sign.
Obtains q₂ = +9.00 × 10⁻⁹ C.

parts.prompt: State whether q₁ and q₂ have the same sign or opposite signs, explaining your reasoning.
parts.expectedAnswer: They have the same sign because their individual electric field vectors must point in opposite directions to cancel between the charges.
workingSteps: Opposite-sign charges produce fields in the same direction everywhere between them.
Therefore q₁ and q₂ must have the same sign.

parts.prompt: Calculate the ratio |q₂ / q₁|.
workingSteps: Distance from q₂ to null point = 0.8 − 0.5 = 0.3 m.

parts.prompt: Hence determine the signed value of q₂.
workingSteps: q₂ is positive (same sign as q₁) with magnitude 0.360 × 2.5 × 10⁻⁸ C.

items.stem: Inside a cryogenic linear Paul-trap alignment fixture, fixed sources q₁ (left, 1.5 × 10⁻⁹ C) and q₂ (right) lie 0.6 m apart. The electric field vanishes at an interior point 0.15 m to the right of q₁.
items.workedSolution: (a) q₁ and q₂ have the same sign so their fields oppose between them. (b) |q₂/q₁| = ((0.6 − 0.15)/0.15)² = (0.45/0.15)² = 9.00. (c) q₂ = +(9.00)(1.5 × 10⁻⁹ C) = +1.35 × 10⁻⁸ C.

markScheme.criterion: States same sign because fields must oppose in the region between the charges.
Uses |q₂/q₁| = ((d − x₀)/x₀)² with d − x₀ = 0.45 m.
Obtains 9.00.
Multiplies q₁ by ratio from (b) with positive sign.
Obtains q₂ = +1.35 × 10⁻⁸ C.

parts.prompt: State whether q₁ and q₂ have the same sign or opposite signs, explaining your reasoning.
parts.expectedAnswer: They have the same sign because their individual electric field vectors must point in opposite directions to cancel between the charges.
workingSteps: Opposite-sign charges produce fields in the same direction everywhere between them.
Therefore q₁ and q₂ must have the same sign.

parts.prompt: Calculate the ratio |q₂ / q₁|.

parts.prompt: Hence determine the signed value of q₂.
workingSteps: q₂ is positive (same sign as q₁) with magnitude 16.0 × 2 × 10⁻⁹ C.

items.stem: Inside an electrostatic dust-accelerator launch stage, planar parallel plates at potentials 840 V and 0 V have separation 0.07 m in vacuum, accelerating a charged bead of mass 2 × 10⁻⁶ kg and charge +5 × 10⁻⁹ C across the full gap. Neglect edge effects and gravitational forces.
items.workedSolution: (a) Uniform field E = V / d = 840 / 0.07 = 1.20 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. (b) Work done by the field W = qV = (5 × 10⁻⁹)(840) = 4.20 × 10⁻⁶ J.

Applies W = qV (or W = qEd).
Obtains 4.20 × 10⁻⁶ J.

items.stem: Along a straight dielectric mounting rod inside an evacuated bell jar, two opposite-sign sources of −8 nC on the left and +4 nC on the right have separation 0.6 m; axial point P is situated 0.4 m from −8 nC. Adopt k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and zero electrostatic potential at infinite distance.
items.workedSolution: (a) V = k(-8 × 10⁻⁹/0.4 + 4 × 10⁻⁹/0.2) = 0 V. (b) At P both fields point to the left, giving E = 449 N C⁻¹ + 899 N C⁻¹ = 1.35 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes signed charges with r₁ = 0.4 m and r₂ = 0.2 m into V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂).
Obtains V = 0 V.
Applies inverse-square law E = k|q|/r² to both sources.
Adds the two collinear field magnitudes.
Obtains 1.35 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left.

items.stem: Inside an ultra-high-vacuum electrostatic calibration chamber, along a 0.75 m baseline between fixed charges −12 nC on the left and −3 nC on the right, point P lies 0.25 m from the left source. markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 1.62 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

items.stem: In a dry-nitrogen micro-electrostatics apparatus, along a 0.6 m baseline between fixed charges +4 nC on the left and +9 nC on the right, point P lies 0.3 m from the left source. Assume vacuum permittivity such that k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Which option states the net electric field vector at P?

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 499 N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

items.stem: On a sapphire isolation substrate inside a cleanroom vacuum stage, along a 0.6 m baseline between fixed charges +9 nC on the left and +3 nC on the right, point P lies 0.2 m from the left source. markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 1.85 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 2.40 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (B).

Point P lies on the connecting axis 0.3 m from the left charge. Assume vacuum permittivity such that k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.3)² = 799 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.5)² = 144 N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 655 N C⁻¹ directed to the left (C).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 655 N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

items.stem: Within a dust-plasma levitation chamber evacuated to low pressure, fixed point charges +2 nC (at x = 0) and +10 nC (at x = 0.6 m) occupy a straight insulating rail. Point P is situated at x = 0.4 m. Adopt the free-space constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Determine the resultant electric field strength and sense at P.
items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.4)² = 112 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.2)² = 2.25 × 10³ N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 2.14 × 10³ N C⁻¹ directed to the left (A).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 2.14 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (A).

items.stem: Inside an electrostatic aerosol-charging test section, a left-hand source of +7 nC and a right-hand source of +3 nC are separated by 0.7 m. An axial test point P is located 0.3 m to the right of +7 nC. Use 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² throughout. Calculate the magnitude and direction of the resultant electric field at P.
items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.3)² = 699 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.4)² = 169 N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 531 N C⁻¹ directed to the right (C).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 531 N C⁻¹ to the right (C).

items.stem: Along the symmetry line of a miniature ion-optics bench, two like-sign point charges of +4 nC and +16 nC are fixed 0.8 m apart, with +4 nC on the left. items.stem: On a low-permittivity PTFE fixture inside an evacuated chamber, fixed point charges +10 nC (at x = 0) and +4 nC (at x = 0.9 m) occupy a straight insulating rail. Point P is situated at x = 0.3 m. Assume vacuum permittivity such that k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electric field at point P?
items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.3)² = 999 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.6)² = 99.9 N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 899 N C⁻¹ directed to the right (A).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 899 N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Along the primary axis of a precision field-mill calibration bench, along a 0.6 m baseline between fixed charges +3 nC on the left and +8 nC on the right, point P lies 0.4 m from the left source. items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.4)² = 169 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.2)² = 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 1.63 × 10³ N C⁻¹ directed to the left (B).

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 1.63 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (B).

items.stem: Inside an ultra-high-vacuum electrostatic calibration chamber, a left-hand source of −12 nC and a right-hand source of −3 nC are separated by 0.75 m. An axial test point P is located 0.25 m to the right of −12 nC. Adopt the free-space constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Which option states the net electric field vector at P?

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 1.62 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

Point P lies on the connecting axis 0.6 m from the left charge. Treat both sources as point charges in vacuum with k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². items.workedSolution: Between like-sign charges, the individual fields at P oppose each other: |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.6)² = 150 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.4)² = 787 N C⁻¹. Subtracting gives |E_net| = 637 N C⁻¹ directed to the left (D).

items.stem: Within a shielded Faraday enclosure used for sensor testing, fixed point charges −7 nC (at x = 0) and −14 nC (at x = 0.8 m) occupy a straight insulating rail. Point P is situated at x = 0.5 m. Model the region as vacuum with Coulomb constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Calculate the magnitude and direction of the resultant electric field at P.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field contributions to obtain 1.15 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (B).

items.stem: On an insulated fused-quartz metrology rail in vacuum, charges +5 nC and +8 nC are mounted 0.4 m apart along a horizontal line, with +5 nC on the left. An axial sensor at exterior point P sits 0.8 m to the right of +5 nC. Treat both sources as point charges in vacuum with k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electric field at exterior point P?
items.workedSolution: Exterior point P is r₁ = 0.8 m to the right of +5 nC and r₂ = 0.8 − 0.4 = 0.4 m to the right of +8 nC. Superposing E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂² gives 520 N C⁻¹ to the right (B).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 0.8 m and r₂ = 0.4 m to obtain 520 N C⁻¹ to the right (B).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 0.75 m and r₂ = 0.25 m to obtain 176 N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

items.stem: Along a straight dielectric mounting rod inside an evacuated bell jar, a point charge −9 nC is fixed at x = 0 and a second point charge −5 nC is fixed at x = 0.3 m. markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 0.6 m and r₂ = 0.3 m to obtain 724 N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

items.stem: Along the central axis of a precision Coulomb torsion module, a point charge +18 nC is fixed at x = 0 and a second point charge −5 nC is fixed at x = 0.6 m. Exterior point P lies further to the right along the positive x-axis at x = 1 m (so P is 0.4 m to the right of −5 nC). Use 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² throughout. What is the resultant electric field at exterior point P?
items.workedSolution: Exterior point P is r₁ = 1 m to the right of +18 nC and r₂ = 1 − 0.6 = 0.4 m to the right of −5 nC. Superposing E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂² gives 119 N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 1 m and r₂ = 0.4 m to obtain 119 N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

items.stem: Across the measurement track of a non-contact Kelvin probe bench, fixed sources −6 nC (left) and −3 nC (right) have separation 0.4 m. Observation point P is positioned on the extended axis beyond the right-hand charge, 0.7 m from −6 nC. Use 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² throughout. What is the resultant electric field at exterior point P?
items.workedSolution: Exterior point P is r₁ = 0.7 m to the right of −6 nC and r₂ = 0.7 − 0.4 = 0.3 m to the right of −3 nC. Superposing E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂² gives 410 N C⁻¹ to the left (B).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 0.7 m and r₂ = 0.3 m to obtain 410 N C⁻¹ to the left (B).

items.stem: Inside an electrostatic aerosol-charging test section, a point charge +9 nC is fixed at x = 0 and a second point charge −2 nC is fixed at x = 0.3 m. Exterior point P lies further to the right along the positive x-axis at x = 0.6 m (so P is 0.3 m to the right of −2 nC). Treat both sources as point charges in vacuum with k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electric field at exterior point P?
items.workedSolution: Exterior point P is r₁ = 0.6 m to the right of +9 nC and r₂ = 0.6 − 0.3 = 0.3 m to the right of −2 nC. Superposing E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂² gives 25.0 N C⁻¹ to the right (C).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 0.6 m and r₂ = 0.3 m to obtain 25.0 N C⁻¹ to the right (C).

items.stem: Along the symmetry line of a miniature ion-optics bench, two collinear point charges of −12 nC (left) and +5 nC (right) are separated by 0.4 m. Point P lies outside the pair to the right of both charges, at a total distance of 0.7 m from the left-hand −12 nC charge. Adopt the free-space constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 0.7 m and r₂ = 0.3 m to obtain 279 N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

items.stem: Inside a cryogenic linear Paul-trap alignment fixture, a point charge +7 nC is fixed at x = 0 and a second point charge +5 nC is fixed at x = 0.35 m. Exterior point P lies further to the right along the positive x-axis at x = 0.7 m (so P is 0.35 m to the right of +5 nC). Model the region as vacuum with Coulomb constant k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the resultant electric field at exterior point P?
items.workedSolution: Exterior point P is r₁ = 0.7 m to the right of +7 nC and r₂ = 0.7 − 0.35 = 0.35 m to the right of +5 nC. Superposing E_x = kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂² gives 495 N C⁻¹ to the right (B).

markScheme.criterion: Uses r₁ = 0.7 m and r₂ = 0.35 m to obtain 495 N C⁻¹ to the right (B).

items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, a point charge q₁ = 2.5 × 10⁻⁸ C sits at x = 0 and an unknown point charge q₂ sits at x = 0.8 m. An axial field scan locates a zero-field null point between them at x = 0.5 m. What is the magnitude ratio |q₂ / q₁|?

markScheme.criterion: Uses q₂ = q₁((d − x₀)/x₀)² with positive sign to obtain +1.35 × 10⁻⁸ C (B).

items.stem: Along a horizontal ceramic support rod in free space, two fixed point charges q₁ and q₂ are separated by 1 m in vacuum, with q₁ = 2 × 10⁻⁹ C on the left. Measurements along the connecting axis show that the resultant electric field is zero at a distance of 0.2 m from q₁. What is the signed charge q₂?
items.workedSolution: An interior null point requires q₁ and q₂ to have the same sign (+). Equating kq₁/x₀² = kq₂/(d − x₀)² with d − x₀ = 0.8 m gives q₂ = q₁((0.8)/(0.2))² = 16.0 × 2 × 10⁻⁹ C = +3.20 × 10⁻⁸ C (D).

markScheme.criterion: Uses q₂ = q₁((d − x₀)/x₀)² with positive sign to obtain +3.20 × 10⁻⁸ C (D).

items.stem: On a low-permittivity PTFE fixture inside an evacuated chamber, fixed sources q₁ (left, 1.2 × 10⁻⁸ C) and q₂ (right) lie 1 m apart. The electric field vanishes at an interior point 0.4 m to the right of q₁. What is the signed charge q₂?

markScheme.criterion: Uses q₂ = q₁((d − x₀)/x₀)² with positive sign to obtain +2.70 × 10⁻⁸ C (B).

items.stem: Along the primary axis of a precision field-mill calibration bench, along a 0.6 m vacuum baseline with q₁ = 1.8 × 10⁻⁸ C at the left end and q₂ at the right end, the net electric field is zero at a point 0.4 m from q₁. What is the magnitude ratio |q₂ / q₁|?
items.workedSolution: At x₀ = 0.4 m, the distance from q₂ is d − x₀ = 0.2 m. Setting |q₁|/x₀² = |q₂|/(d − x₀)² gives |q₂/q₁| = (0.2/0.4)² = 0.250 (C).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ((d − x₀)/x₀)² = (0.2/0.4)² = 0.250 (C).

items.stem: Inside an ultra-high-vacuum electrostatic calibration chamber, two fixed point charges q₁ and q₂ are separated by 0.8 m in vacuum, with q₁ = 2.7 × 10⁻⁸ C on the left. markScheme.criterion: Uses q₂ = q₁((d − x₀)/x₀)² with positive sign to obtain +3.00 × 10⁻⁹ C (C).

items.stem: In a dry-nitrogen micro-electrostatics apparatus, a point charge q₁ = 9 × 10⁻⁹ C sits at x = 0 and an unknown point charge q₂ sits at x = 0.5 m. An axial field scan locates a zero-field null point between them at x = 0.3 m. What is the magnitude ratio |q₂ / q₁|?
items.workedSolution: At x₀ = 0.3 m, the distance from q₂ is d − x₀ = 0.2 m. Setting |q₁|/x₀² = |q₂|/(d − x₀)² gives |q₂/q₁| = (0.2/0.3)² = 0.444 (D).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ((d − x₀)/x₀)² = (0.2/0.3)² = 0.444 (D).

items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, fixed sources q₁ (left, 2.5 × 10⁻⁸ C) and q₂ (right) lie 0.8 m apart. The electric field vanishes at an interior point 0.5 m to the right of q₁. What is the signed charge q₂?
items.workedSolution: An interior null point requires q₁ and q₂ to have the same sign (+). Equating kq₁/x₀² = kq₂/(d − x₀)² with d − x₀ = 0.3 m gives q₂ = q₁((0.3)/(0.5))² = 0.360 × 2.5 × 10⁻⁸ C = +9.00 × 10⁻⁹ C (A).

markScheme.criterion: Uses q₂ = q₁((d − x₀)/x₀)² with positive sign to obtain +9.00 × 10⁻⁹ C (A).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ((d − x₀)/x₀)² = (0.8/0.4)² = 4.00 (B).

items.stem: Inside a university physics Van de Graaff calibration tunnel, two fixed point charges q₁ and q₂ are separated by 0.6 m in vacuum, with q₁ = 9 × 10⁻⁹ C on the left. Measurements along the connecting axis show that the resultant electric field is zero at a distance of 0.36 m from q₁. What is the signed charge q₂?
items.workedSolution: An interior null point requires q₁ and q₂ to have the same sign (+). Equating kq₁/x₀² = kq₂/(d − x₀)² with d − x₀ = 0.24 m gives q₂ = q₁((0.24)/(0.36))² = 0.444 × 9 × 10⁻⁹ C = +4.00 × 10⁻⁹ C (C).

markScheme.criterion: Uses q₂ = q₁((d − x₀)/x₀)² with positive sign to obtain +4.00 × 10⁻⁹ C (C).

items.stem: Within a cleanroom charged-microparticle levitation cell, planar parallel plates at potentials 1000 V and 0 V have separation 0.025 m in vacuum, accelerating a charged bead of mass 2.8 × 10⁻⁶ kg and charge +1.4 × 10⁻⁸ C across the full gap. What uniform electric field magnitude acts across the space between the parallel electrodes?
items.workedSolution: For uniform parallel plates, E = V / d = 1000 / 0.025 = 4.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Between parallel titanium electrodes inside a beam-diagnostics chamber, a uniform electrostatic gap of width 0.04 m operates with 320 V across its parallel plates while a carrier (q = +8 × 10⁻⁹ C, m = 4 × 10⁻⁶ kg) traverses from the high-potential plate to the 0 V plate. How much electrical work is done by the electric field on the particle as it crosses from the 320 V plate to the 0 V plate?
items.workedSolution: Electrical work done across the full potential difference is W = qΔV = (8 × 10⁻⁹)(320) = 2.56 × 10⁻⁶ J (C).

items.stem: In an evacuated parallel-plate velocity-calibration gap, inside an evacuated cell of gap width 0.08 m biased at 1600 V, a charged aerosol particle of mass 3 × 10⁻⁶ kg and charge +1.5 × 10⁻⁸ C travels from the +1600 V electrode to the 0 V collector. Neglecting fringing at the plate edges, calculate the uniform electric field strength in the gap.
items.workedSolution: For uniform parallel plates, E = V / d = 1600 / 0.08 = 2.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Across the planar anode–cathode spacing of a vacuum photo-tube, flat parallel plates spaced 0.018 m apart establish a 270 V potential drop as a micro-carrier (mass 2.5 × 10⁻⁶ kg, charge +3 × 10⁻⁸ C) moves from the positive plate to the earthed 0 V plate. items.workedSolution: Electrical work done across the full potential difference is W = qΔV = (3 × 10⁻⁸)(270) = 8.10 × 10⁻⁶ J (A).

items.stem: Inside an electrostatic dust-accelerator launch stage, planar parallel plates at potentials 840 V and 0 V have separation 0.07 m in vacuum, accelerating a charged bead of mass 2 × 10⁻⁶ kg and charge +5 × 10⁻⁹ C across the full gap. What uniform electric field magnitude acts across the space between the parallel electrodes?
items.workedSolution: For uniform parallel plates, E = V / d = 840 / 0.07 = 1.20 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: In a time-of-flight mass spectrometer extraction stage, a uniform electrostatic gap of width 0.03 m operates with 240 V across its parallel plates while a carrier (q = +2.5 × 10⁻⁸ C, m = 4 × 10⁻⁶ kg) traverses from the high-potential plate to the 0 V plate. How much electrical work is done by the electric field on the particle as it crosses from the 240 V plate to the 0 V plate?
items.workedSolution: Electrical work done across the full potential difference is W = qΔV = (2.5 × 10⁻⁸)(240) = 6.00 × 10⁻⁶ J (A).

items.stem: Inside a cathode-ray oscilloscope vertical deflection assembly, inside an evacuated cell of gap width 0.05 m biased at 400 V, a charged aerosol particle of mass 5 × 10⁻⁶ kg and charge +3 × 10⁻⁸ C travels from the +400 V electrode to the 0 V collector. Neglecting fringing at the plate edges, calculate the uniform electric field strength in the gap.
items.workedSolution: For uniform parallel plates, E = V / d = 400 / 0.05 = 8.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Across the parallel accelerating gap of a semiconductor ion implanter, flat parallel plates spaced 0.04 m apart establish a 600 V potential drop as a micro-carrier (mass 3 × 10⁻⁶ kg, charge +1.5 × 10⁻⁸ C) moves from the positive plate to the earthed 0 V plate. items.workedSolution: Electrical work done across the full potential difference is W = qΔV = (1.5 × 10⁻⁸)(600) = 9.00 × 10⁻⁶ J (C).

items.stem: Between the flat brass electrodes of a Millikan electrostatic cell, two parallel conducting plates separated by 0.025 m are maintained at a potential difference of 150 V (from 150 V on the left plate to 0 V on the right plate). A positively charged droplet of charge +4 × 10⁻⁸ C and mass 4 × 10⁻⁶ kg is released at the 150 V plate. Ignore edge effects. What is the magnitude of the uniform electric field between the plates?
items.workedSolution: For uniform parallel plates, E = V / d = 150 / 0.025 = 6.00 × 10³ V m⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Within a medical linear-accelerator pre-injector gap, a uniform electrostatic gap of width 0.045 m operates with 360 V across its parallel plates while a carrier (q = +5 × 10⁻⁸ C, m = 2 × 10⁻⁶ kg) traverses from the high-potential plate to the 0 V plate. How much electrical work is done by the electric field on the particle as it crosses from the 360 V plate to the 0 V plate?
items.workedSolution: Electrical work done across the full potential difference is W = qΔV = (5 × 10⁻⁸)(360) = 1.80 × 10⁻⁵ J (C).

items.stem: Between two planar molybdenum grids of an ion-thruster prototype, inside an evacuated cell of gap width 0.03 m biased at 900 V, a charged aerosol particle of mass 3.6 × 10⁻⁶ kg and charge +1.8 × 10⁻⁸ C travels from the +900 V electrode to the 0 V collector. Neglecting fringing at the plate edges, calculate the uniform electric field strength in the gap.
items.workedSolution: For uniform parallel plates, E = V / d = 900 / 0.03 = 3.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Between precision-spaced invar plates in a metrology vacuum tank, across a 0.035 m vacuum gap with potential difference 1400 V, a deuteron carrying +0 C and mass 0 kg accelerates from rest from the positive plate to the 0 V plate. markScheme.criterion: Sums signed scalar potentials kq₁/0.3 + kq₂/0.6 = 375 V (C).

markScheme.criterion: Sums signed scalar potentials kq₁/0.3 + kq₂/0.2 = −285 V (D).

items.stem: Along the primary axis of a precision field-mill calibration bench, two stationary charges of −7 nC on the left and +3 nC on the right have separation 0.5 m, with point P marked 0.2 m from the left source. Model the charges in free space (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²), taking V = 0 at infinity. What is the electric potential at point P?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential is a signed scalar: V = k(q₁/r₁ + q₂/r₂) with r₁ = 0.2 m and r₂ = 0.3 m. Thus V = −315 V + (89.9 V) = −225 V (B).

markScheme.criterion: Sums signed scalar potentials kq₁/0.2 + kq₂/0.3 = −225 V (B).

items.stem: Along a straight dielectric mounting rod inside an evacuated bell jar, two opposite-sign sources of −8 nC on the left and +4 nC on the right have separation 0.6 m; axial point P is situated 0.4 m from −8 nC. Adopt k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and zero electrostatic potential at infinite distance. Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the left: E = 449 N C⁻¹ + 899 N C⁻¹ = 1.35 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 1.35 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 719 N C⁻¹ to the right (D).

items.stem: Across the test region of a high-impedance electrometer bench, opposite point charges +6 nC (left) and −18 nC (right) are fixed 0.8 m apart. Point P lies on the connecting axis 0.2 m from +6 nC, where the scalar electric potential vanishes. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and define electric potential to be zero at infinity. markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Along the reference baseline of an electrostatic beam-steering rig, fixed charges +4 nC at x = 0 and −4 nC at x = 0.4 m establish a zero-potential point P on the axis at x = 0.2 m. With zero potential set at infinity in vacuum, use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the right: E = 899 N C⁻¹ + 899 N C⁻¹ = 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (A).

items.stem: Inside an electrostatic aerosol-charging test section, two opposite-sign sources of +2 nC on the left and −8 nC on the right have separation 0.5 m; axial point P is situated 0.1 m from +2 nC. Adopt k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and zero electrostatic potential at infinite distance. Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the right: E = 1.80 × 10³ N C⁻¹ + 449 N C⁻¹ = 2.25 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (B).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 2.25 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right (B).

items.stem: Inside an ultra-high-vacuum electrostatic calibration chamber, along the 0.8 m line segment between +3 nC (left) and −9 nC (right), point P sits 0.2 m from the left source. Model the charges in free space (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²), taking V = 0 at infinity. Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the right: E = 674 N C⁻¹ + 225 N C⁻¹ = 899 N C⁻¹ to the right (C).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 899 N C⁻¹ to the right (C).

items.stem: Along the optical axis of a benchtop ion-trap demonstration rig, opposite point charges −5 nC (left) and +15 nC (right) are fixed 1 m apart. Point P lies on the connecting axis 0.25 m from −5 nC, where the scalar electric potential vanishes. Adopt k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and zero electrostatic potential at infinite distance. Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the left: E = 719 N C⁻¹ + 240 N C⁻¹ = 959 N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 959 N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

items.stem: Within an evacuated spacecraft charge-control test cell, opposite point charges −7 nC (left) and +7 nC (right) are fixed 0.7 m apart. Point P lies on the connecting axis 0.35 m from −7 nC, where the scalar electric potential vanishes. Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and define electric potential to be zero at infinity. Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the left: E = 514 N C⁻¹ + 514 N C⁻¹ = 1.03 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 1.03 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left (C).

items.stem: Within a dust-plasma levitation chamber evacuated to low pressure, fixed charges −2 nC at x = 0 and +6 nC at x = 0.8 m establish a zero-potential point P on the axis at x = 0.2 m. With zero potential set at infinity in vacuum, use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². Although the electric potential at P is zero, what is the resultant electric field at P?
items.workedSolution: Even though V = kq₁/r₁ + kq₂/r₂ = 0 at P, the potential gradient dV/dx is non-zero because both opposite charges drive a positive test charge to the left: E = 449 N C⁻¹ + 150 N C⁻¹ = 599 N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

markScheme.criterion: Recognizes E != 0 when V = 0 and sums collinear contributions to obtain 599 N C⁻¹ to the left (D).

items.stem: On a sapphire isolation substrate inside a cleanroom vacuum stage, along a 0.9 m axis between +6 nC on the left and −14 nC on the right, a +2.5 nC probe particle rests momentarily at point P (0.3 m from +6 nC). markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = k(q₁/0.3 + q₂/0.6) = −30.0 V (B), independent of q_test.

items.stem: Within a dust-plasma levitation chamber evacuated to low pressure, along a 0.5 m axis between +8 nC on the left and −3 nC on the right, a +3.2 nC probe particle rests momentarily at point P (0.2 m from +8 nC). Model the charges in free space (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²), taking V = 0 at infinity. What is the electric potential at P due to the two fixed source charges?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential at P depends only on the source charges: V = k(q₁/0.2 + q₂/0.3) = 360 V + (−89.9 V) = 270 V (B).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = k(q₁/0.2 + q₂/0.3) = 270 V (B), independent of q_test.

Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and define electric potential to be zero at infinity. What is the electric potential at P due to the two fixed source charges?
items.workedSolution: Electric potential at P depends only on the source charges: V = k(q₁/0.2 + q₂/0.3) = 315 V + (−89.9 V) = 225 V (B).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates V = k(q₁/0.2 + q₂/0.3) = 225 V (B), independent of q_test.

items.stem: Within a shielded Faraday enclosure used for sensor testing, along a 0.6 m axis between +6 nC on the left and +9 nC on the right, a −1.5 nC probe particle rests momentarily at point P (0.2 m from +6 nC). items.stem: Along the central axis of a precision Coulomb torsion module, fixed point charges +5 nC (at x = 0) and +12 nC (at x = 0.8 m) occupy a straight insulating rail. Point P is situated at x = 0.5 m. Treat both sources as point charges in vacuum with k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Both positive sources repel a positive test charge placed at P, so the left charge pushes rightward while the right charge pushes leftward. (b) |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.5)² = 180 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.3)² = 1.20 × 10³ N C⁻¹. Subtracting the opposing vectors yields 1.02 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: States that a positive test charge between like-sign sources experiences opposite forces from the left and right charges.
Evaluates E = k|q|/r² at r₁ = 0.5 m and r₂ = 0.3 m.
Subtracts the two opposing field magnitudes.
Obtains 1.02 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left.

parts.prompt: Explain why the electric fields produced by the two negative charges oppose each other at point P.
parts.expectedAnswer: Both negative sources attract a positive test charge placed at P, so the left charge pulls leftward while the right charge pulls rightward.
workingSteps: Both negative sources attract a positive test charge placed at P, so the left charge pulls leftward while the right charge pulls rightward.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude and state the direction of the resultant electric field at point P.
workingSteps: Net field E = 1.15 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right.

items.stem: Along a straight dielectric mounting rod inside an evacuated bell jar, a left-hand source of +12 nC and a right-hand source of +5 nC are separated by 0.8 m. An axial test point P is located 0.3 m to the right of +12 nC. Use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² for free-space electrostatic interactions.
items.workedSolution: (a) Both positive sources repel a positive test charge placed at P, so the left charge pushes rightward while the right charge pushes leftward. (b) |E₁| = k|q₁|/(0.3)² = 1.20 × 10³ N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = k|q₂|/(0.5)² = 180 N C⁻¹. Subtracting the opposing vectors yields 1.02 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right.

markScheme.criterion: States that a positive test charge between like-sign sources experiences opposite forces from the left and right charges.
Evaluates E = k|q|/r² at r₁ = 0.3 m and r₂ = 0.5 m.
Subtracts the two opposing field magnitudes.
Obtains 1.02 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the right.

items.stem: In a dry-nitrogen micro-electrostatics apparatus, fixed sources +12 nC (left) and −4 nC (right) have separation 0.4 m. Observation point P is positioned on the extended axis beyond the right-hand charge, 0.8 m from +12 nC. Assume vacuum permittivity such that k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Because P lies to the right of both opposite-sign charges, one source repels a positive test charge rightward while the other attracts it leftward, so their fields oppose. (b) Using r₁ = 0.8 m and r₂ = 0.4 m, |E₁| = 169 N C⁻¹ and |E₂| = 225 N C⁻¹, giving resultant E = 56.2 N C⁻¹ to the left.

markScheme.criterion: States opposite directions with correct test-charge reasoning.
Identifies r₁ = 0.8 m and r₂ = 0.4 m.
Applies signed vector superposition kq₁/r₁² + kq₂/r₂².
Obtains 56.2 N C⁻¹ to the left.

items.stem: Inside an electrostatic ink-droplet test nozzle in vacuum, inside an evacuated cell of gap width 0.08 m biased at 800 V, a charged aerosol particle of mass 6 × 10⁻⁶ kg and charge +2 × 10⁻⁸ C travels from the +800 V electrode to the 0 V collector. Neglect edge effects and gravitational forces.
items.workedSolution: (a) Uniform field E = V / d = 800 / 0.08 = 1.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. (b) Work done by the field W = qV = (2 × 10⁻⁸)(800) = 1.60 × 10⁻⁵ J.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes V = 800 V and d = 0.08 m into E = V / d.
Obtains 1.00 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹.
Applies W = qV (or W = qEd).
Obtains 1.60 × 10⁻⁵ J.

Uses inverse-square magnitudes at r₁ = 0.3 m and r₂ = 0.4 m.
Combines the two collinear field vectors with proper directions.
Obtains 1.22 × 10³ N C⁻¹ to the left.
